question.text: Calculate the height $h$ of the cylinder above given that its volume is $32\pi \,\textrm{m}^3$ and its radius is $2\,\textrm{m}.$
question.explanation:
The volume of a cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ is given by

\[ V = \pi r^2h. \]

Substituting $V = 32\pi\,\textrm{m}^3$ and $r = 2\,\textrm{m}$ into the formula and solving for $r,$ we get

\begin{align*} V &= \pi r^2 h \\[3pt] 32\pi &= \pi (2)^2 h \\[3pt] 4\pi h &= 32\pi \\[3pt] h &= 8 \,\textrm{m}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding a Dimension of a Cylinder Given Its Volume

question.text: Find an expression for the volume $V$ of a cylinder in terms of $r$ given that $\dfrac{r}{h} = 7,$ where $r$ is the radius of the base and $h$ is the height of the cylinder.
question.explanation:
Our goal is to express $V$ in terms of $r.$ Therefore, we need to isolate $h$ in the above equation: \begin{align*} \dfrac{r}{h} & = 7 \\[5pt] r &= 7 h \\[5pt] \dfrac{r}{7} & = h\\[5pt] h & = \dfrac{r}{7} \end{align*}

The volume of a cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ is given by \[ V = \pi r^2h . \]

Therefore, substituting $h = \dfrac{r}{7}$ into the formula, we get \begin{align} V & = \pi r^2 h\\[5pt] & = \pi r^2 \cdot \dfrac{r}{7} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\pi r^3}{7}. \end{align}

example.title: Finding an Expression for a Dimension of a Cylinder Given a Proportion

question.text: Find an expression for the height $h$ of a cylinder in terms of its volume $V$ given that the ratio of the radius of the base to the height of the cylinder is $\dfrac{1}{3}.$
question.explanation:
Using the fact that the ratio of the radius $r$ of the base to the height $h$ is $\dfrac{1}{3},$ we have that \begin{align} \dfrac{r}{h} &=\dfrac{1}{3}. \end{align}

Our goal is to express $h$ in terms of $V.$ Therefore, we need to isolate $r$ in the above equation, which we do using cross-multiplication: \begin{align} \dfrac{r}{h} & =\dfrac{1}{3}\\[5pt] 3r & = h\\[5pt] r & = \dfrac{h}{3} \end{align}

The volume of a cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ is given by \[ V = \pi r^2 h. \]

Therefore, substituting $r = \dfrac{h}{3}$ into the formula, we get \begin{align*} V &= \pi r^2 h \\[5pt] V &= \pi \left( \dfrac{h}{3}\right)^2 \cdot h \\[5pt] V & = \pi \cdot \dfrac{h^2}{9} \cdot h\\[5pt] V &= \dfrac{\pi h^3}{9} \\[5pt] h^3 &= \dfrac{9V}{\pi} \\[5pt] h &= \sqrt[3]{ \dfrac{9V}{\pi}}. \end{align*}
